text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty page fired for service `inference-pipeline-prod` (P0) — latency threshold breached (>3000ms avg over 1m). Trigger: request-aggregator-queue. Assigned to: @eng-oncall. Incident ID: PD-11984
incident-bot: PagerDuty: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-11984

jordan: ack — oncall here, picking this up. seeing a bunch of 5xx and long tail latency in the initial graphs.

alice: whoa, that service should be bound to infra-sre for routing. did someone change the PD binding? we keep getting pages to eng-oncall during night shifts.

oncall-rotations-bot: check: service `inference-pipeline-prod` -> PD service binding: `team: eng-oncall` (binding-id: bnd_7892). expected: `infra-sre` per rotations config v3.1. Last binding update: 2026-02-25T21:12:09Z by carla-sre via api.

sam: confirmed — PD binding looks wrong. I'm seeing duplicate pages from PD because both `inference-pipeline-prod` and a legacy alias `inference-pipeline` are firing.

jordan: ok, immediate plan: 1) suppress duplicate paging rules in PD to stop fanout, 2) apply short-term traffic reroute to `inference-shard-b` region, 3) investigate why requests spiked. i'll take 1+2 now.

carla-sre: wait on rolling restarts; that can make tail latency worse. prefer traffic-shift + health-marking. also runbook: do not restart aggregator pods unless CPU is pegged.

jordan: doing suppression:
```bash
# suppress duplicate rules in PD (10m)
pdcli incidents mute --service inference-pipeline-prod --duration 10m --reason "duplicate fanout"
```

jordan: applying routing fallback to inference-shard-b:
```bash
redwood-route set-policy inference-pipeline-prod --fallback inference-shard-b --reason "mitigate latency spike"
```

oncall-rotations-bot: rotation-scan: active schedule mismatch detected. PD service `inference-pipeline-prod` points to `eng-oncall` because legacy-binding `bnd_7892` still exists. canonical rotation file -> infra-sre-night. Suspect: binding override via API key `svc-deploy-key` on 2026-02-25.

alice: that API key belongs to our automation for canary rollouts — seems like an automation job accidentally updated service binding during a yaml apply.

sam: customer-impact assessment so far: 12% of requests in the last 10m had latency >2s, ~3% returned 5xx. Services impacted: storefront-search (user-facing), autosuggest. Estimated affected users: subset of EU region traffic routed through shard-a.

jordan: mitigation status: suppression active, fallback in place (traffic ~40% shifted), dashboards show p50 down from 3.4s -> 1.1s, p95 still ~2.8s. throttled background batch jobs for queue `priority-low` to reduce load.

carla-sre: can someone paste the PD service binding snippet that shows the misroute? need it for the post-incident patch.

alice: here is the problematic payload from the API audit log:
```json
{
  "binding_id": "bnd_7892",
  "service": "inference-pipeline-prod",
  "assigned_team": "eng-oncall",
  "updated_by": "svc-deploy-key",
  "updated_at": "2026-02-25T21:12:09Z",
  "change_reason": "automated-deploy:bind-service"
}
```

sam: thanks. i'll open a quick PD change to rebind to infra-sre and set a guard to prevent automation from changing binding without manual approval.

oncall-rotations-bot: patch proposed: rebind `inference-pipeline-prod` -> `infra-sre`. suggested approver: carla-sre.

jordan: rebind done (manual override) and confirmed in PD UI. patched guard deployed: `binding-write` permission now requires `automation:bind-approval` flagged.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident PD-11984 updated: responder changed to `infra-sre`. escalation level reset. pages suppressed.

carla-sre: good. next, we need a short incident timeline for customers and ops: what do we tell affected teams?

alice: draft for customer-facing blurb: "We briefly saw increased inference latency affecting search/autosuggest for certain EU customers. Traffic was rerouted and the affected requests are back to normal. Root cause: an automated deployment accidentally changed PagerDuty service binding causing operator routing delays. No model data was exposed."

sam: internal impact note: 12% high-latency requests, 3% 5xx, mitigation by traffic shift and suppression reduced user impact within 12 minutes.

jordan: handing off to alice for follow-up and postmortem — my shift ends at 02:15 UTC. leaving a note in the incident runbook and adding cross-check to PD CI.

alice: ack takeover, I will: 1) file postmortem, 2) add CI test that verifies PD binding after deploy, 3) add alert to detect PD-binding drift, 4) limit automation key scopes.

carla-sre: thanks team. after-action quick list:   
- rollback problematic automation rule (carla)   
- CI test for PD binding (alice)   
- PD runbook update + deck for oncall (sam)   
- Add telemetry alert for sudden-binding-changes (eng infra)

incident-bot: Incident PD-11984 marked: mitigated (status update) — monitoring for regression.

jordan: final check: p95 trending down to 1.1s, error rate back to baseline. I'll close my ack and leave the incident in alice's hands.

alice: thanks — i'll run the postmortem template and assign owners. closing updates in 24h once we have root cause verified. :white_check_mark:
